evaluation_target.statement: Prevent omission of required braking maneuvers in the hazard-relevant driving situation.
evaluation_target.rationale: The safety goal explicitly requires preventing omission of required braking maneuvers, and the hazard describes the adverse outcome when braking is not performed in time to avoid collision.

phenomenon_of_interest.statement: Vehicle braking behavior in the hazard-relevant operational situation, specifically whether braking maneuver execution is required and performed in time to avoid collision with a road user or obstacle.
phenomenon_of_interest.scope: Straight-ahead driving on a less frequented single-lane road at 50 km/h in good weather with a pedestrian running across the street 20 m in front of the ego vehicle, and the associated perception/planning/control state relevant to deciding and executing braking to avoid collision.
phenomenon_of_interest.rationale: The hazard defines the operational situation and collision outcome, while FR-7 and FR-7.1 state that the system shall perform a braking maneuver and start braking within a bounded time after obstacle detection in a dangerous zone.

distinctions.contrast_a: A required braking maneuver is initiated and executed
distinctions.contrast_b: A required braking maneuver is omitted
distinctions.rationale: The safety goal and functional braking requirement distinguish successful braking from omission; collapsing these would remove the ability to evaluate whether the hazard is being prevented.

distinctions.dimension: Temporal relation between obstacle detection and braking initiation
distinctions.contrast_a: Braking starts within the required/expected time after obstacle detection in the dangerous zone
distinctions.contrast_b: Braking starts too late after obstacle detection to avoid collision
distinctions.rationale: FR-7.1 explicitly introduces a timing relation between obstacle detection and braking start; collapsing timely versus late braking would lose information needed to evaluate omission-risk relevant braking performance.

distinctions.contrast_a: An obstacle/road user is detected on or close to the trajectory in the hazard-relevant situation
distinctions.contrast_b: No such obstacle/road user is detected
distinctions.rationale: FR-7, FR-7.1, FR-7.2, and FR-7.2.4 make braking contingent on obstacle detection and distance to objects on or close to the trajectory; collapsing presence versus absence would remove the trigger context for evaluating whether braking is required.

orrs.obligation: An admissible Observable Representation shall preserve whether a required braking maneuver is initiated/executed versus omitted.
orrs.distinguishability_criterion: The representation must allow the two braking outcomes to remain distinguishable as separate states or categories.

orrs.obligation: An admissible Observable Representation shall preserve the ordering and temporal separation between obstacle detection and braking initiation sufficiently to distinguish timely braking from late braking.
orrs.distinguishability_criterion: The representation must retain a distinguishable temporal relation between detection and braking start; timely and late initiation must not collapse into the same state.

assumptions.statement: Obstacle detection provides the event reference needed to relate braking start to the detection moment.

revalidation_conditions.condition: If the basis for triggering braking changes from obstacle detection to another event or if the detection pipeline changes materially.

orrs.obligation: An admissible Observable Representation shall preserve whether an obstacle or road user is present on or close to the trajectory in the hazard-relevant situation, so that braking necessity can be assessed.
orrs.distinguishability_criterion: The representation must distinguish obstacle/road-user present versus absent for the relevant trajectory context.

assumptions.statement: The operational notion of 'dangerous zone' and 'objects on or close to the trajectory' remains the decision context for braking.

revalidation_conditions.condition: If the dangerous-zone definition or the trajectory-relative obstacle criterion is revised.
